role: Editable learner glossary copy. Map existing vocabulary IDs before promotion; preserve vocabulary:v1 and prior response history. These four core terms do not replace additional definitions within each lesson.

terms.definition: Something you want to explore or enjoy doing.
An ability demonstrated through an action, rather than only a claim.
Something that matters to you about how or where you work.
A specific observation or record that supports a claim.
A summary of an occupation's duties, conditions and preparation for a stated place and time.
A task that is part of a role.
A feature of where, when or how the work happens.
Canada's National Occupational Classification, which groups occupations; its codes identify groups, not personal ability.
A sequence of preparation and decisions that can lead toward a direction.
Something that must be completed before a later course or step.
A formal record of a qualification, such as a certificate, diploma or degree.
A benefit you give up or a cost you accept when choosing an option.
The relationship between people seeking work and organizations seeking workers in a place and period.
An estimate about a future pattern, not a guaranteed outcome.
A position an employer is seeking to fill.
The occupation group, place, period and measure that a statement actually covers.
An ordered sequence in which each required earlier course permits the next step.
Stated as a condition that must be met for the particular route.
Suggested as helpful, without being stated as compulsory.
A planned time to review evidence and decide whether a plan needs changing.
Work performed for an employer under the arrangement's stated terms.
Organizing a venture that provides a product or service and carries its own costs and risks.
Money received by a venture before subtracting its expenses.
Revenue left after the included expenses are subtracted; it is not the same as revenue.
The time and resources actually available after existing commitments.
Time or money left available for variation or unexpected needs.
Something given preference when resources cannot cover every option.
A specific change to a plan in response to evidence or a changed condition.
A notice describing a role, its duties and what an applicant is asked to provide.
Notes about what someone actually did in a particular situation.
Something a person did that can be described specifically.
What happened after the action, limited to what the record supports.
Instructions and information for a particular period of work.
Authority to carry out a specified action.
Something that could cause harm.
Information that should be accessed or shared only for an authorized purpose.
An interview question asking for an example of how someone acted.
The task or part of the work a person was expected to handle.
Practising an answer so you can check its clarity and accuracy.
Building professional connections to exchange information and learn about opportunities.
A problem that prevents the next required step from proceeding.
A task or condition that must be completed before another step can start.
Done one task after another.
Done during the same period by people or resources that can work independently.
A specific action or result noticed in the record.
An explanation of what an observation may suggest.
An ability or habit that needs further development.
A possible career direction to investigate, not a final verdict from one experience.
A minimum legal requirement applying to an employment arrangement within its stated scope.
Permission given by the person whose permission is required.
Oversight by an appropriate person under the applicable rule or procedure.
The authority and scope under which a law or rule applies.
Something that could cause harm.
The possibility and seriousness of harm in the circumstances.
A measure used to remove a hazard or reduce exposure to it.
Instruction and practice needed to perform a task safely and appropriately.
A protection or entitlement provided by the applicable rules.
An obligation attached to a role or situation.
A clear record of relevant facts, dates and actions.
A specific issue to raise with supporting facts and an appropriate requested action.
Unfair adverse treatment connected to a protected ground in an area covered by human-rights law.
A characteristic protected by the applicable human-rights legislation.
An adjustment considered to address a protected need within the applicable legal duties and limits.
A conclusion drawn from facts that must be distinguished from what was directly observed.
Earnings before deductions for the stated pay period.
An amount taken from gross pay under the statement's listed categories.
Gross pay minus the current deductions.
A total accumulated from the beginning of the year to the stated date.
A limit or condition that a decision must respect.
Something that shapes how a person sees or chooses an option.
Something required to meet a stated purpose or obligation in the case.
An option someone likes, which still needs to be weighed against the case's limits.
A plan showing income and how money will be used.
When money enters and leaves an account.
Money already in the account at the start of the period.
The amount by which available money is less than a required payment or target.
An amount needed at the beginning of an agreement or purchase.
An amount paid repeatedly over the stated period.
Money held temporarily that is returned only when the stated return conditions are met.
All costs included within the comparison's stated period and assumptions.
A temporary price that applies only for its stated period and conditions.
An agreement lasting for a specified period under its terms.
An agreement continuing by monthly periods under its stated cancellation terms.
An amount that the agreement says may be payable when ending it under specified conditions.
The purchase and continuing costs of keeping and using an item.
An initial expense needed to begin using a purchase or service.
A calculated amount based on stated information and assumptions.
Something relevant that is not known or not guaranteed.
The amount borrowed or still owed before the interest for the period is added.
The charge for borrowing money under the agreement's rate and method.
An asset pledged as security for a debt.
A person who shares responsibility for a debt under the agreement.
A rate expressed for a one-year period.
Interest calculated on the stated original principal for the specified time.
The part of a year used when matching time to an annual rate.
Money paid back, including the amounts required by the agreement.
Repaying a debt over time through scheduled payments.
The total amount paid at a scheduled time, which may include interest and principal.
The portion of a payment that reduces the amount borrowed.
The debt left after the period's interest and payment are applied.
The smallest payment due under the supplied agreement for that period.
Money paid beyond the required minimum.
A plan for allocating payments while respecting each debt's terms.
Using borrowed money for an investment, leaving a repayment obligation even if its value falls.
Whether the payment and timing fit available resources and other commitments.
Credit that spreads or delays payment for a purchase under stated terms.
The point by which a payment or action must occur in the case.
An option whose availability and relevant conditions are supplied or verified.
A rate that stays the same during the agreement's specified period.
A rate that can change according to the agreement's terms.
A specified point when the rate changes in the supplied scenario.
A check of whether a plan remains workable under a stated less favourable condition.
A loan secured on property.
The buyer's own contribution toward the purchase price.
The period during which the mortgage agreement's particular conditions apply before renewal or repayment.
A stated allowance for extra repayment without the charge that would otherwise apply.
A named purpose, target amount and deadline for money being set aside.
Money added to a goal or account.
Accessible money set aside for unexpected needs.
The total available for all the named goals together.
The next-best alternative given up when making a choice.
How readily money or an asset can be accessed for use, considering conditions or losses.
A gain or loss relative to the money invested, considering relevant costs.
A purpose that receives money before a lower-priority option under the case's conditions.
An asset or financial product held, such as a deposit, bond, stock or fund.
The legal and tax framework in which eligible money or investments are held.
How long before money is expected to be needed.
Spreading investments across different holdings to reduce concentration; it does not eliminate risk.
A rise in the general level of prices over time.
What an amount of money can buy at a particular price level.
The money amount stated without adjusting it for changes in purchasing power.
A money amount expressed at a comparison period's price level.
How a shared amount is divided among purposes.
A period in a plan during which the same allocation rule applies.
Only the remaining amount needed to finish a target, leaving the rest available for another purpose.
A tool, information source or service that can answer a specific planning question.
A condition a plan relies on.
A difference between what was planned and what actually happened in the case.
A change or date that signals the plan should be checked.
A recalculated future result using the updated balance and stated conditions.
Information left by online activity, sharing and transactions.
Sharing or keeping only the information needed for a particular purpose.
A sign-in protection requiring an additional factor beyond a password.
The people who can see a post or information under the actual sharing settings.
Pretending to be another person or organization to gain trust.
A deceptive attempt to obtain information or access by posing as a trusted source.
Checking through a route obtained separately from the suspicious message.
A feature that raises a concern and calls for verification; it is not by itself a complete proof.
Information or access has been revealed to someone who should not have it.
Information or access has actually been used improperly.
An active signed-in connection that may remain open under a service's rules.
The genuine provider's process for regaining or protecting account access.
A claim made about a product, service, price or agreement.
A charge the buyer must pay to obtain the advertised offer under the supplied terms.
A disagreement with the seller about the transaction, product or agreement.
An action that may address a problem under the relevant rules; it is not automatically guaranteed.
An ordered response to an incident that addresses security, evidence and appropriate reporting.
The organization controlling the account or service involved.
A notice asking potential creditors to take additional identity-verification steps.
A record separating planned actions, actions taken and confirmed results.
